newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks start sharply higher on Dow gain.
newsitem.headline: French stocks start sharply higher on Dow gain.

text.p: French shares entered the week with a jump of just over one percent at the open but then gave back some of the opening gains.

Traders said the market took heart from last Friday's 102 point rise on on the U.S. Dow Jones index and a strong dollar and expected more active business with the return of many market professionals after the holidays.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 18.23 points or 0.80 percent at 2,300.99 at 0916 GMT, while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 16 at 2,304 from Friday's settle.
Dollar-earners benefit from strength in the U.S. currency, with blue chips Elf Aquitaine up 0.98 percent at 476.10 francs and LVMH rising 1.13 percent to 1,429.
Insurer Axa gains 0.94 percent to 333.10, continuing Friday's gain on the back of the profit contribution from Australian unit National Mutual.
Utility group Cie Generale des Eaux also among top turnover stocks, up 1.10 percent at 645 francs, helped by Friday's news of asset sales and debt reduction for 1996.

Subsidiaries of rival Lyonnaise des Eaux, Degremont and Sita, both up sharply. The gains may be on the back of hopes of Lyonnaise buying out minorities, similar to its operation on its Elyo heating subsidiary.
Synthelabo rises 2.63 percent to 585. Merger and takeover speculation in the pharmaceuticals sector may be behind the rise, traders said.
